niphal.sense_hint: simple (this root has no attested qal; niphal serves as its basic/citation stem -- the participle itself functions as a substantive, the same pattern as H3009 יגב)

notes: Strong's derives this word "from an unused root meaning to roll to pieces" -- WLC nonetheless tags all 3 occurrences (Prov.18.8, 26.20, 26.22, all the identical form נִרְגָּן) as a genuine niphal active participle (morph="HVNrmsa"), not a plain noun, so it clears the bar for inclusion.
"Talebearer" and "whisperer" trimmed to one clause: both are the same evidenced sense worded twice (all three citations are one repeated word/proverb), not two distinct senses.

Related: H3859 (להם, "swallow greedily") already in the dataset shares its two citations with this word's own (Prov.18.8 / 26.22 -- the same verse, repeated), and its notes already reference this word's KJV rendering ("talebearer") in passing.
